question: Should bundled Policy own a stable, user-authored routing-conformance contract, or should this remain outside the bundled plugin until maintainers define that product boundary?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally opt-in and uses the existing routing resolver, but it adds durable policy syntax, Doctor check IDs, evidence semantics, documentation, and strictness/comparison behavior that cannot be selected safely by automated review alone.

options.title: Sponsor the Policy contract
options.body: Keep the routing section in the bundled Policy plugin, rebase it, and review its documented schema and compatibility semantics as a supported operator contract.

options.title: Defer to external policy tooling
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers do not want bundled Policy to own routing probes and evidence semantics.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the Policy contract
recommendation.body: Keep the routing section in the bundled Policy plugin, rebase it, and review its documented schema and compatibility semantics as a supported operator contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the linked problem statement and the proposed Policy contract, so they are the available routing contact while a current-main owner is identified.
